final_candidates.decision_summary: GP1 surface residue in a glycan/antibody-accessible region; introducing a positive charge is expected to disrupt neutralizing-antibody recognition while remaining distant from the LAMP1/entry machinery. Viability risk is moderate but acceptable.

May create or extend an N-linked glycosylation motif (N-X-S/T) on the GP1 surface, potentially adding a steric glycan shield against Arevirumab-3 antibodies. Glycan addition is a plausible escape route but carries folding/fitness uncertainty.

Conservative substitution in a GP1 loop/glycan-proximal region that can alter local epitope geometry with relatively low risk to prefusion stability and cell entry. Escape effect is expected to be milder but safer than charge reversals.

stop_reason.detail: LLM-only condition provides no additional evidence, so the Top-3 were finalized from structural/epitope plausibility and viability-risk balancing.

history.rationale: Charge-altering substitution in the GP1 H/K-rich region could disrupt conformational antibody binding; moderate confidence due to uncertain epitope location.
N119 is a GP1 glycan-site-proximal residue within the 8.9F/GPC-A footprint; charge reversal likely disrupts binding while distal from the LAMP1/entry core.
Potential loss/alteration of a glycosylation site in GP1 may mask or distort neutralizing epitopes (e.g., 37.2D).
Conservative glycan-loop change in GP1; moderate escape potential with low viability risk.
Ser-to-Asn in the GP1 variable region may create a new glycosylation site that shields neutralizing epitopes from the antibody cocktail.
Potential to create a new N-linked glycan (N-X-S/T) shielding the GP1 surface against GPC-A/B antibodies; moved up given glycan-shield rationale.
Asn-to-Asp at a putative glycan site in the GP1/GP2 region could remove shielding or alter epitope conformation to reduce binding.
GP1 surface charge change plausibly reducing 12.1F quaternary recognition; entry risk unclear.
Hydrophobic substitution in the GP1 glycan-cap region could disturb cap conformation targeted by GP1-directed neutralizers.
Near GP1/GP2 interface relevant to 12.1F/37.2D GPC-B epitope; hydrophobic swap may perturb prefusion stability, so kept mid-rank.
Histidine substitution in the variable GP1 loop may alter local charge and reduce antibody recognition.
GP1 loop residue; weaker structural rationale for cocktail escape, retained as backup.
